summary: Chicago water-intake crib about 3.3 miles east of Monroe Harbor, finished in the 1890s with an iron light tower. Closed to visitors; its future is disputed.

structures.note: Completed 1891 (LighthouseFriends) or 1894 (Preservation Chicago); see the story's Building the light.
Red skeletal iron tower with a silver lantern on the crib (LighthouseFriends). The sources read do not date it.

staffing.note: On standby service for years before the city's 2015 capital-plan demolition proposal (Preservation Chicago).

access.note: Not open to the public (US Lighthouse Society archive); tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Best viewed from a boat or plane (LighthouseFriends). Owned by the Chicago Department of Water Management.

events.note: Completed in 1891 (LighthouseFriends); Preservation Chicago gives construction from 1887 to 1894.
Steam heating plant installed in the crib, keeping the well room at a steady temperature.
Submarine cable laid from Chicago Harbor light to power the crib's light; a two-room addition built on the crib (LighthouseFriends reports that the Bureau of Lighthouses noted both in 1932).
Two power and control cables laid for Four Mile Crib in the Twelfth District's cable programme (Lighthouse Service Bulletin).
Final crew of keepers withdrawn from duty on the Chicago water cribs.
Security systems installed on all the Chicago intake cribs.
City's four-year capital programme, announced in 2015, plans demolition of the crib.
Demolition work put out for bid, according to the preservation group; the group says it was never awarded.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree and the story states each without choosing: Preservation Chicago gives construction 1887 to 1894; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS archive give 1891; the preservation group gives service in 1892 and completion in 1894. Costs also disagree: LighthouseFriends gives $472,890.93 for the stone and brick crib alone and $1,526,143.68 for the system; Preservation Chicago gives $429,000 in 1894 dollars for the crib and tunnel. The record's tower entry (built 1898, 9.0 m) is not matched by the USLHS page (established 1891) or LighthouseFriends (which dates 1898 to the steam heating plant); the 9.0 m height and the 1898 tower date need checking. The light characteristic conflicts: LighthouseFriends describes a white flash every three seconds; the record says Fl W 15s (ENC). The 1877 and 1881 Lighthouse Board notes in LighthouseFriends concern the Two-Mile Crib, not this crib. No Lighthouse Board or Commissioner text on this light is in the local corpus (the 1891 to 1901 Board reports do not mention it); the 1932 cable entry comes via LighthouseFriends, which cites the Commissioner. The 1934 Bulletin cable table is OCR'd; the Four Mile row was matched by text (Four Mile Crib, 2 cables) and its length and conductor figures were not used. The 1901 Life-Saving Service report has an undated table entry, 'Capsized outside the 4-mile crib with four men on board', but the OCR does not place it at a station; not used. Chronicling America searches for Four Mile Crib in Illinois papers, 1889 to 1935, returned no hits. No keeper is named in any source read, and the USLHS roster lists none; the story says so rather than naming anyone. The preservation group's site is run by an interested party: its capital-plan figures were not checked against the City's capital programme documents. Its status after about 2021 is unknown; the crib's current condition and the city's current plan need a check before publication. The Wikipedia article on Chicago's water cribs lists the crib as scheduled for demolition, but Wikipedia is used here only as a lead and is not cited.
